items.title: The Sewing Machine on the Porch
items.pitch: Help a parent start a small dress shop at home. The work may give an adult child a trade and the savings to leave, closing the household business your gift once made busy.

present_hook.what_you_notice: A porch has an unused sewing-machine space, and old papers record a parent who could not afford the start-up work. The adult child's later departure came without a shared local business.

clues.line: {A} priced a sewing venture in {year}. Child {B} never worked at the proposed shop.

window.notes: A is B's parent. Require A's verified sewing skill, an approved Main Street home-workspace plan, actual unmet demand and B's later interest in the trade. Present must be at least 28 years later.

interventions.how_it_looks: Fund the documented equipment and approved home-workspace shortfall.

ripples.headline: Home Dress Shop Opens Beside a Family Porch
ripples.body: {A} opened a permitted dress shop in the approved home workspace. Customers began bringing fitting appointments to a formerly quiet porch.

ripples.headline: Adult Child Joins the Family Dress Shop
ripples.body: {A} hired adult child {B} on agreed wages. The new worker gained paid experience and a personal savings reserve.

ripples.headline: Child Takes an Outside Offer as Home Dress Shop Retires
ripples.body: {B} accepted a verified job outside town while {A} chose retirement. The home dress shop closed after settling its final orders and expenses.

fails.headline: Home Sewing Venture Stops Before Opening
fails.body: The venture planned by {A} did not secure enough paid orders within its opening window. Some equipment was resold at a loss.

present_day.best: In {now}, the porch has no operating dress-shop counter and the business records show a productive run followed by retirement. B has a recorded voluntary departure, not a scripted death or abandonment.
present_day.worst: First-step failure creates no family employer. The actual gift balance and equipment expenses remain accounted for, and B's later choices follow ordinary history.
present_day.twist: The gift can help the child afford a life elsewhere rather than preserve a busy family home. A successful upbringing does not promise lifelong proximity.

npc_lines_after.line: I am proud of the work that got my child that offer. The porch is quieter than I expected.

Step 1 requires A's actual skill, viable paid demand, funded equipment and lawful home-business use. Record the founded shop ID and separate it from household ownership.
Step 2 requires B adult, consenting and qualified for the paid tasks, with real wages and available work. Neither biological relation nor high ambition guarantees employment.

Add close_founded_business: resolve only the scenario dress shop, require A still owning it and voluntarily retiring, settle orders, staff and creditors and remove its operating signage. B's move requires a real outside offer, affordable relocation and voluntary acceptance; A's ten percent debit is actual uncovered closure expense, not punishment for the child leaving. Gate A's line on step 3, A alive and B still living elsewhere.
items.era_notes: Use sewing equipment and garment demand available in the relevant decade. Keep the outside employer unnamed.
items.why_fun: The same porch changes from quiet to busy and back again. The empty counter can mark a successful chapter rather than a failed gift.

items.title: The Oven That Heated the Block
items.pitch: Invest in a bakery's heat-recovery proposal. Warmth that once escaped through the roof may eventually serve nearby buildings, while the old fuel yard loses its customers.

present_hook.what_you_notice: A bakery vents unused heat beside buildings using separate boilers. An unfunded recovery proposal sits near the fuel yard's old delivery map.

clues.line: {A} proposed recovering oven heat in {year}. The financing failed, and every building kept its separate fuel deliveries.

window.notes: shop belongs to A; B owns the bound local fuel yard. Require a technically feasible heat-recovery design, suitable nearby demand, viable backup heating and B's real reliance on the affected delivery accounts. Present must be at least 29 years later.

interventions.how_it_looks: Fund the inspected pilot recovery equipment and its maintenance reserve.

ripples.headline: Bakery Pilot Captures Heat Once Lost Through the Roof
ripples.body: The bakery run by {A} commissioned an inspected heat-recovery pilot. Measured usable output replaced estimates in the project file.

ripples.headline: Measured Bakery Heat Supports a Shared Heating Line
ripples.body: A funded shared connection supplied suitable nearby buildings with recovered heat. Independent backup heating remained part of the approved design.

ripples.headline: Fuel Yard Closes After Its Delivery Base Shrinks
ripples.body: The fuel yard run by {B} closed after sustained losses of delivery accounts to the functioning shared heating service. Customers retained the service and backup arrangements recorded in their contracts.

fails.headline: Bakery Recovery Pilot Produces No Usable Commissioned Output
fails.body: The proposed recovery installation at the bakery run by {A} failed its commissioning tests. Actual project expenses remained recorded, but no heating benefit was credited.

present_day.best: In {now}, a shared heating connection and its service equipment are visible on the block, while the bound fuel yard has closed. Actual warmth depends on current supply, operation and backup systems.
present_day.worst: First-step failure produces no shared heat or scenario fuel-yard closure. Later heating improvements remain possible through ordinary history.
present_day.twist: Less wasted heat can reduce a whole block's fuel demand while removing a local livelihood. Efficiency does not create replacement work automatically.

npc_lines_after.line: I understand why they wanted the warmth. I used to know every door on that delivery route.

Add fuel merchant as a business kind with real inventory, delivery accounts, staff and prices; bind B's original yard ID.

Add recover_heat: require era-supported engineering, actual measured output, food-safe separation, inspection and funded operation. Debit investment through actual costs once and preserve unspent capital on failure.

Step 2 requires an active viable heat source, lawful connections, a funded costed design, adequate temperatures and independent safe backups. Use actual recovered energy; never multiply heat or promise a warm block after the bakery closes.

close_owned_business requires B still owning the yard and actual sustained insolvency after customer shifts and reasonable adaptations. Settle staff, stock and creditors normally. Gate B's line on step 3, B alive and the original delivery memories.
items.era_notes: Use only technically supported heat-recovery and distribution designs for the event decade; otherwise reject the scenario.
items.why_fun: The ripple travels through pipes rather than a family tree. A quiet fuel yard makes a successful efficiency project less abstract.

items.title: The Chess Table by the Door
items.pitch: Introduce a lonely older player to a child who wants to learn chess. The lessons may become a toy-shop club and then an indoor venue, while the original free drop-in table becomes a reserved space.

present_hook.what_you_notice: A scratched chess table sits unused outside a public hall. A school request for a volunteer teacher never found a match.

clues.line: {B} asked for chess lessons in {year}. {A} offered to teach, but the requests were never paired.

window.notes: Require A's real willingness and chess competence, B's supervised request, the existing free public table and a later viable vacant toy-shop site. Present must be at least 28 years later.

interventions.how_it_looks: Arrange a supervised lesson at the public table after both agree.

ripples.headline: Volunteer and Pupil Give the Hall Table a New Routine
ripples.body: {A} began supervised chess lessons with pupil {B}. The outdoor table acquired regular games without an entry fee.

ripples.headline: Former Pupil Opens a Toy Store with a Chess Club
ripples.body: {B} opened a funded toy store and organized a regular chess club. The remembered lessons provided a beginning, not a guarantee of business success.

effects.reserve_table: the bound free hall chess table

ripples.headline: Indoor Chess Room Adds Scheduled Reservations
ripples.body: The club organized by {B} opened a funded indoor room with a permitted use agreement for the old hall table during scheduled sessions. Casual users lost unrestricted access at those times.

fails.headline: Friendly First Lesson Does Not Become a Regular Arrangement
fails.body: {A} and {B} enjoyed a supervised game but could not arrange continuing lessons. The public table remained available under its existing rules.

present_day.best: In {now}, a toy-store premises and indoor chess room exist, with a posted reservation schedule at the original public table. Current club activity and ownership follow replay.
present_day.worst: First-step failure creates no taught chess proficiency, store or club through this chain. B can learn elsewhere and A can teach others under ordinary history.
present_day.twist: A free intergenerational lesson grows into a better-equipped institution, but institutional scheduling limits the table that originally welcomed anyone.

npc_lines_after.line: I like that people still play. I used to be able to sit down here without checking whose session it was.

Apply direct interventions once. Persist people, objects, businesses, sites, funds and knowledge; invalidate descendants on replay. Recheck survival, ownership and resources. Gate present text and after-lines by recorded outcomes, surviving features and informed living speakers. No forced unrelated events or duplicate rewards.

Add teach_skill: track actual supervised lessons and incremental proficiency, never grant mastery from one meeting. Require appropriate child safeguarding and consent; no invented parental relationship.
Step 2 requires B adult, adequate business skill and capital, a lawful site and actual club demand. establish_event records staffing, venue, budget and recurring sessions that may lapse.

Step 3 requires an active funded club, lawful construction and a public authority's reviewed limited table-use agreement, with accessible public hours retained. Add reserve_table: restrict only listed club-session slots, update signage and interactions and expire reservations when the club closes. The indoor room does not swallow the outdoor table or duplicate it. The after-line requires a living former casual user and an active reservation.
items.era_notes: Use physical chess sets and posted schedules throughout. Online play is optional later and never required for the chain.
items.why_fun: A scratched tabletop becomes a place with a history the player helped create. Its reservation sign shows how even a welcoming tradition can change as it grows.

items.title: The Numbers Before the Drawing
items.pitch: Tell a resident the winning number you learned from the original town raffle. A funded department store may follow, while a smaller shop loses customers to a fortune that arrived by an impossible route.

present_hook.what_you_notice: The raffle archive records a winning number and an unclaimed prize. A never-funded department-store proposal sits beside an open small bakery.

clues.line: The number drawn in {year} went unclaimed. {A} never found capital for the larger store.

window.notes: Require a lawful fixed-number raffle with the baseline prize unclaimed, A able to afford the available numbered ticket, the actual drawing unaffected by intervening choices, a vacant department-store site and B's bakery competing with its planned food counter. Present must be at least 27 years later.

interventions.how_it_looks: Disclose the verified original drawing number before its still-available ticket can be bought.

ripples.headline: Previously Unclaimed Raffle Number Gains a Buyer
ripples.body: {A} bought the available winning-number ticket and lawfully claimed the funded raffle prize. The buyer declined to explain the unusual confidence behind the purchase.

ripples.headline: Raffle Winner Opens the Long-Proposed Department Store
ripples.body: {A} opened a funded department store after years of planning and capital management. Its licensed food counter joined the clothing and household departments.

ripples.headline: Small Bakery Closes as Department-Store Counter Expands
ripples.body: The bakery run by {B} closed after sustained customer losses to the department store founded by {A}. The larger store's success left a smaller counter empty.

fails.headline: Resident Declines an Unexplained Raffle Tip
fails.body: {A} declined the unusual number tip and discussed the odd encounter with neighbor {B}. The bound winning ticket remained unclaimed under the baseline drawing.

present_day.best: In {now}, a department-store building occupies the proposed site and B's bakery has a recorded closure. The raffle register records a legitimate claim where the original branch recorded none.
present_day.worst: On first-step failure, A receives no prize and no scenario store follows. The player cannot obtain a payout merely by repeating the same information.
present_day.twist: An unexplained windfall can finance useful shops while displacing an existing baker. The lucky resident's prosperity does not make the original small business obsolete by moral right.

npc_lines_after.line: I still have the number written down. I cannot explain why that visitor knew it before the drawing.

proposed_verbs.does: Privately disclose one verified original-branch raffle result to A before ticket sales close. Add that communicated fact and its uncertain provenance to A's knowledge; do not force a purchase, create a ticket or alter the drawing. Reject if the ticket is sold, the drawing has changed or the player lacks the actual prior result.

new_rules_needed: Choose years and independent rolls keyed by seed, scenario ID, intervention year, bound IDs and step. after_years is elapsed from intervention. Check prerequisites before rolling; failure or ineligibility stops descendants without reversing earlier effects. fails is the first-step complement, never an additional roll. Apply direct interventions once. Persist people, objects, businesses, sites, funds and knowledge; invalidate descendants on replay. Recheck survival, ownership and resources. Gate present text and after-lines by recorded outcomes, surviving features and informed living speakers. No forced unrelated events or duplicate rewards.

Bind the raffle event, available numbered ticket, fixed seeded drawing and a real escrowed prize. The first-step roll represents A voluntarily purchasing that exact ticket; the drawing is not rerolled. award_prize debits escrow, verifies the legal ticket and claims the existing prize once, never mints a fraction of A's money.

Keep original-branch knowledge separate from current-branch facts. A knows what the player said, not all erased history; changes that alter the actual drawing invalidate the prediction. Track ticket identity and claims so visits and object transfers cannot duplicate payouts.

Add department store as a business kind with separately costed departments, food licensing, staffing and actual demand. Founding requires saved prize capital after real living costs and a permitted vacant site, not automatic growth from winning.

Step 3 requires both original owners still operating their bound businesses and actual sustained competitive losses at B's bakery after adaptations. close_owned_business settles staff and creditors normally. Gate A's line on step 3, A alive and the retained memory of the tip.
items.era_notes: Use a simple local numbered raffle with a genuinely fixed drawing supported by the simulation. If raffle law or mechanics do not support this setup, reject rather than guarantee magical gambling knowledge.
items.why_fun: The player uses remembered history rather than a larger wallet. The claimed-prize entry and changed storefronts expose the cost of that unfair advantage.
